chunks: Abu Basir narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:
Regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic,
"Then let them complete their prescribed duties."

He عليه السلام said: "It refers to what occurs from a man during the state of his ihram. Then when he enters Mecca, performs tawaf, and speaks good words, that is an expiation for that which had occurred from him."

key_terms.إِحْرَامِهِ: his state of consecration for hajj or 'umrah
key_terms.تَفَثَهُمْ: their prescribed acts of removing the effects of ihram
key_terms.طَافَ: he performed tawaf around the Ka'bah
key_terms.كَفَّارَةً: an expiation that wipes away what occurred
key_terms.مَكَّةَ: Mecca, the sacred city entered during the pilgrimage rites

ai.seo_question: What does «ثُمَّ لْيَقْضُوا تَفَثَهُمْ» mean in relation to ihram and tawaf?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the verse about completing tafath as referring to what occurs to a pilgrim during the state of ihram. When he enters Mecca, performs tawaf, and speaks good words, this serves as an expiation for what occurred from him in that state.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3030 - Abu Basir narrated from Abu Abdullah (as)
regarding the saying of Allah (swt), the Almighty:
"Then let them complete their prescribed duties" (Surah Al-Hajj 22:29)

.
Imam (as) said: "It refers to what happens to a person during the state of ihram. When he enters Mecca, performs the tawaf, and speaks good words, that becomes an expiation for what occurred during his ihram."
